# Assets

**All art and sound in this game is generated by code at startup.** There are no image or
audio files in this folder, only data:

| Folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `rooms/` | `world.json` (room list and start room) and one JSON file per room |
| `fonts/` | Liberation Serif (SIL Open Font License 1.1, see `fonts/OFL.txt`) |

## How the procedural art works

1. `phantom.art.SpriteFactory.build()` runs every *painter* once:
   `CharacterPainter`, `CreaturePainter`, `BossPainter`, `PropPainter`, `NpcPainter`,
   `TilePainter`, `BackgroundPainter`, `UiPainter`.
2. Each painter draws layered silhouettes (polygons, tapered Bezier strokes, ellipses,
   radial glows) onto a `Canvas`, a small software rasteriser that works at 4x resolution.
   A rim light pass lights the upper-left edges.
3. The canvas is downsampled (anti-aliasing), converted to a `Pixmap` and packed into a
   texture atlas with `PixmapPacker`. A white silhouette of every creature frame is packed
   too, for hit flashes.
4. Gameplay code asks for sprites by name: `ctx.art().sheet("crawler")`.

You can preview all art without starting the game:

```
./gradlew :core:artPreview -PoutDir=/tmp/phantom-art
```

## Replacing the art with hand-drawn sprite sheets

An artist can replace any sprite without touching gameplay code:

1. Draw the frames at **2 texels per world unit** (for example, the player sprite is
   64x64 world units, so 128x128 pixels per frame), facing **right**, with the feet at the
   same height in every frame.
2. Pack them with the libGDX TexturePacker into `assets/sprites/sprites.atlas`, naming the
   regions `<sprite>#<frame>`, e.g. `player_run#0` ... `player_run#5`.
3. In `SpriteFactory.build()`, load that atlas and, for each region found, register it
   instead of the painted version (the `SpriteSheet` class only needs the regions, the
   logical size and the foot offset).

Sprite names and frame counts used by the game: `player_idle` (4), `player_run` (6),
`player_jump`, `player_fall` (2), `player_dash`, `player_cling`, `player_focus` (2),
`player_rest`, `shade`, `crawler` (3), `flutterer` (4), `sentinel` (2), `brute` (6),
`gnarlwarden` (6), `warden` (5), `heart_core` (3), `heart_tendrils`, `npc_ossian`,
`npc_quill`, `npc_seraphine`, `npc_vesper`, `bench`, `shrine` (2), `relic`, `shard`,
`cache`, `rock`, `gear`, `bolt`, `slash` (3), `cracks` (3), `decor_<region>`,
`eruption_<region>`, `tile_<region>_<part>`, `mask_full`, `mask_empty`, `soul_orb`,
`soul_fill`, `shard_icon`, plus the textures `bg_<region>_<0..3>`, `shaft`, `fog`,
`soft` and `vignette`.

## Room file format

```json
{
  "id": "r1_gate", "name": "Fallen Gate", "region": "WHISPERING_ROOTS", "map": [0, 40],
  "legend": { "E": {"type": "door", "id": "east", "to": "r1_hollow", "toDoor": "west"} },
  "tiles": [ "#####...", "#P..K..E", "########" ]
}
```

Tiles (top row first): `#` rock, `.` air, `=` one-way ledge, `^` spikes, `B` breakable wall,
`g` boss gate, `~` water, `m` Hollow Mist (hurts). Markers: `P` player start, `K` bench,
`c` crawler, `f` flutterer, `s` sentinel, `b` brute, `r` falling rock, `L` light.
Any other character must be defined in `legend` (doors, NPCs, shops, shrines, relics,
shard caches, bosses). Doors sit on the left or right edge and are three tiles tall.
Run `./gradlew test` after editing a room: `LevelValidationTest` fails if the map can no
longer be completed.
